title: Settlement 1: Key Terms, Types and Shapes
subject: Geography
description: Settlement key terms, rural and urban settlements, and nucleated, dispersed and linear shapes.
author: L.M.

cards.back:
Important buildings

cards.back:

cards.front: What do linear settlements often follow?

questions.question: What is a stakeholder?
options: The land around where a settlement is built
A person that has an interest or an opinion on something
The main uses or activities in a settlement
The ranking of settlements by their size
questions.explanation: A stakeholder is a person that has an interest or an opinion on something.

questions.question: Which word describes 'the ranking of settlements by their size'?
questions.explanation: The settlement hierarchy ranks settlements by their size.

questions.question: An urban settlement normally has a population of over...
questions.explanation: An urban settlement is built-up, large in size and normally has over 10,000 people.

questions.question: Which settlement shape often follows a road, river, railway or valley bottom?
questions.explanation: Linear settlements are long and thin, like a line, and follow a road, river, railway or valley.

questions.question: Which settlement shape has lots of transport routes meeting at a central point?
questions.explanation: Nucleated settlements are circular or semi-circular, with routes meeting at a central point.

questions.question: Foxdale is an example of a...
questions.explanation: Foxdale is a rural settlement. Douglas is an urban settlement.
